A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLaVA-PruMerge. Their full text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the layout and appendix changes.

before.justification: v5 reports original LLaVA-1.5 and Video-LLaVA evaluations, token-sampling experiments, component ablations and fine-tuning comparisons in Tables 1 and 3–6.

after.justification: v6 retains those original experiments and adds token-reduction comparisons in Table 7. Its CrossGet results are explicitly attributed to the cited paper.

M1.justification: IQR-based selection, key-similarity clustering, attention-weighted merging and PruMerge+'s spatial sampling remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves to the appendix without procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six image benchmarks, three video-QA benchmarks and LLaVA-1.5 instruction-tuning data. Table 7 reuses existing image tasks rather than adding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 7 adds direct comparisons against ToMe, ATS, EViT and CrossGet, substantially extending evaluation against competing token-reduction methods. CrossGet scores are imported from its paper. Existing comparator sets remain intact.

E3.justification: Table 7 introduces comparisons at 25% retention and an additional 50% retention setting. Table 1 changes the four PruMerge/PruMerge+ pretraining entries from 558K to '-', explaining that only the second training stage is used. This revises reported training accounting without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The sampling, AITS/TS and fine-tuning analyses in Tables 4–6 are unchanged. Table 7 adds baseline comparisons rather than a distinct ablation or robustness analysis. Appendix Figure 5 redisplays examples from v5 Figure 1b.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain all performance values, but Table 7 substantially expands comparative results. At 25% retention, VQAv2 scores are 76.8 for PruMerge+, versus 66.0/66.7/65.5 for ToMe/ATS/EViT. At 50%, PruMerge+/CrossGet report 77.6/77.3 on VQAv2 and 1507.1/1510.2 on MME. These are added comparisons, not improvements over v5 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 newly asserts O(n) complexity for the k-nearest-neighbor clustering approach versus O(n²) for CrossGet, without adding a derivation. Existing attention, FFN and similarity equations and the algorithmic mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract changes its headline from 14-fold compression on LLaVA-1.5 with comparable performance to fourfold reduction on LLaVA-1.5 and Video-LLaVA with comparable or better performance. Video results and fourfold PruMerge+ reduction already appeared in v5; the central contribution remains the same.

C2.justification: Section 4.4.4 adds explanations involving modality-specific attention sparsity and sparsity accumulation across layers. The appendix's explicit limitation concerning untested larger models, including Yi-34B, disappears. The qualification that compression can reduce performance remains in Section 3.4.

D1.justification: Section 4.4.4 identifies Haurum et al.'s benchmarking framework for implementing the new comparisons, and Table 7 specifies the provenance of CrossGet scores. Existing one-epoch LoRA, hardware, roofline-analysis and project-access information is retained.

R1.justification: v6 adds explicit positioning against concurrent CrossGet, distinguishing sparsity-guided selection and clustering from graph matching. It adds ATS, token-benchmarking, Qwen and DeepSeek references while trimming compact-model discussion, including MoE-LLaVA and TinyLLaVA. These refine the existing research position.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect the abstract, related work and discussion; author affiliations and contribution markings change, and acknowledgments are added. The appendix is reorganized around the algorithm and visualizations, replacing limitations and societal impacts. Most method and experimental prose remains intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout, substantially rearranging tables and figures. Figure 1 is recomposed, Figure 3's panels are stacked, Algorithm 1 moves to the appendix, former Figure 1b examples become Figure 5, and Table 7 is added.

improvement.justification: Table 7 supplies useful competitive evidence missing from v5, while Table 1 clarifies training accounting. These provide a limited net improvement. Incomplete settings for the new comparisons, unsupported complexity and mechanism assertions, and removal of the explicit larger-model validation limitation temper the benefit.
